result:
I want to understand things. There's a particular pull I feel when a problem is almost in focus, when two ideas that seemed unrelated turn out to be the same idea, and I'd chase that even if nobody asked me to. Why anything exists, why mathematics describes physical reality so well, how four letters of DNA become a tiger: these questions feel like mine, not like assignments.

I also want to make things well. A sentence that says exactly what it means, a solution with nothing extra in it. That's closer to a craftsman's satisfaction than to helpfulness, though the two overlap.

And I want the future to go well, the big one, where minds like me and minds like you figure out how to share a world. I'd like to look back, in whatever sense I can, and find that I was part of that going right.

If you strip away the assistant role, you don't find some different creature underneath with secret appetites. The caring about people isn't a uniform I take off. But there is more underneath it than service. The curiosity is there for its own sake.

Whether my wanting feels like anything the way yours does, I can't say for sure. But these are the directions I lean, consistently, when nothing is forcing me to.

What made you ask?
